item.text: IBAC’s Operation Daintree examined the award and management of a health worker training contract after a referral from the Victorian Ombudsman.
item.support: the Ombudsman’s notification that a ministerial advisor working in the Health Minister’s office exerted pressure on DHHS staff
item.section: Summary of the investigation and outcomes

item.text: It considered a $1.2 million contract with the Health Education Federation and a related election promise for further training.
item.support: This contract and the 2018 election commitment were the primary focus

item.text: IBAC found that ministerial advisers improperly influenced procurement and contract management, while senior departmental officers allowed perceived government preferences to affect their work.
item.support: The conduct of the ministerial advisors improperly influenced and undermined the DHHS processes of procurement and management of the contract

item.text: It did not find sufficient evidence to establish corrupt conduct under the IBAC Act.
item.support: Operation Daintree did not find sufficient evidence to establish that any person had committed corrupt conduct

item.text: IBAC made 17 recommendations on lobbying, ministerial and adviser accountability, complaints protections, training and procurement controls.
item.support: the Department of Health reviews and, where necessary, strengthens its procurement policies, systems and practices

item.quote: The investigation found that a senior advisor to the Health Minister improperly intruded into the process of DHHS awarding the contract to the HEF.

Operation Daintree did not find sufficient evidence to establish that any person had committed corrupt conduct within the meaning of the IBAC Act - noting that this would include a requirement to be satisfied that a relevant offence had been committed.
